notes:
Summary: EmberForge builds an opinionated CI/QA pipeline and wants a code-assistant that can run tests/lints and stream build logs back into the developer IDE in near-real time. Primary ask is tool/function-calling for safe execution of repo-level test harnesses inside a sandboxed runtime and returning structured results (exit codes, junit/coverage, lint diffs).

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2026-01-20: initial inbound from developer advocate; demo request.
- 2026-02-18: product demo (Fireflies ff_2026-02-18_emberforge-demo) — showed streaming token experience + function-calling concept.
- 2026-02-25: security engineering kickoff; shared Redwood security FAQ (drive link).
- 2026-03-02: architecture review with infra team (ff_2026-03-02_security_call).
- 2026-03-08: asked for POC access to private sandbox + example test runner. POC target: 2-week smoke + perf.

Requirements / constraints (customer language, shorthand):
- Workloads: low-latency completion for IDE autocomplete (sub-40ms token latency target), streaming build logs for live feedback, on-demand test runs invoked via function call.
- Concurrency: expect up to ~500 concurrent dev sessions during peak day; typical daily active 120-200.
- Model/versioning: must pin model per-repo and have deterministic outputs for CI; want rollback/version pinning and per-repo model profiles.
- Sandboxing: ephemeral containerized execution, strict no-egress by default, per-run resource limits, filesystem snapshots for reproducible runs. "Cannot risk CI machines calling out" — platform sec.
- Observability: persistent build logs (S3 compatible), token-level cost breakdown, per-request tracing for test runs.
- Security: SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS for secrets, 30-day retention by default but need flexible retention for compliance. Some EU customers require residency in eu-west.
- Function-calling contract: ability to call runner.test_run(payload) -> returns structured result {status, exit_code, artifacts[]}, plus streaming log events back to client. Need support for tool-calls that return binary artifacts (e.g., tarball) or signed artifact URLs.
- Cost sensitivity: medium-high. Engineering seats expensive; want optimize recommendations to reduce per-test token costs (batching for offline analyses, cheaper model for lint-only runs).

POC scope / success criteria:
- Realize a POC where an IDE plugin triggers a function call that spins up a sandboxed runner, executes test suite, streams stdout/stderr back into the editor within 3s of invocation, and returns structured junit + coverage.
- Latency SLOs: first token stream < 300ms after runner starts; steady streaming throughput adequate for 10MB/minute log flows.
- Security: egress blocked, encryption of artifacts at rest, audit events for every function call.
- Operational: model pinning per-repo works; can fallback to cheaper model for linting jobs automatically.

Quotes / call snippets:
- "We need deterministic CI outputs — if completion changes the test runner behavior we fail builds." — SRE manager.
- "If it's going to execute code, it must be hermetic and observable." — Head of Security.
- "Low-latency streaming is non-negotiable for dev experience." — Senior Product Manager.

Integrations requested:
- GitHub Actions/GitLab CI triggers, ability to map function calls to existing runners.
- Artifact storage: S3-compatible (prefers internal object store).
- Audit export to SIEM (Splunk).

Next steps (short):
- Grant POC creds to EmberForge engineering (owner: Jordan Park).
- Provide sandbox template (example runner image + function-calling contract) by 2026-03-15.
- Security sign-off checklist to be returned by EmberForge infosec (target 2026-03-22).

Open blockers (short):
- Legal review of code-execution liability and OSS license scanning.
- Internal budget approval for dedicated capacity (estimated ARR range provided).
- Clarify EU residency options for subset of customers.

Stubs / links: drive://emberforge/rdw-internal/poctest-plan ; thread-CA1234efg ; INF-2917.

AE notes (Jordan): POC looks promising — strong product fit for Redwood Optimize (recommend quantized models + routing for lint/test mix). Keep SE close for sandbox runtime tuning (Maya Chen).
